title: Python: a del target is a binding for scope purposes; the walker records none, so 6d, R4, M1, LIT, K1 and every single-binding rule miscount (DEC-303 (a40))
description:
WIDENED by DEC-303 (a40) item 1 (opum-ai/opum-doc#2006, 2026-11-26T09:51:38Z): 'A del target is a binding for scope purposes. The Python language reference (Execution model, binding of names) says: A target occurring in a del statement is also considered bound for this purpose (though the actual semantics are to unbind the name). So the missing del is a defect against rules in force ((a22) item 2: every binding counts), as (a31) item 3 classes D1 and D2. It is not a new design question. If glyph-cli's reproduction confirms the hole, the fix records del targets as bindings everywhere the walker counts bindings (6d, R4, ALIAS, M1, LIT and any other single-binding rule), on its own task with red/green fixtures. If the reproduction finds no hole, the fixture says so and the task closes.' It joins (a36) item 1(i): the fresh blind sample does not draw until this has landed. Corpus diff: count and bin moves need no ruling; any in-repo edge created or removed on the pins comes to opum-doc before the clear.

REPRODUCTION (confirmed on origin/dev e13f2f8, R4 at c84ad89; found by the GCLI-113 round 2 review F4). Classes C and D each define run. Source A: def g(): / def h(): / def k(): / nonlocal x; x = D() / k() / def h2(): / nonlocal x; x = C() / h() / x.run() / del x. The site x.run() resolves to C.run (rule 6d on the single binding that arrived with origin h2); at run time h() runs k, so x is a D. Source B adds def h3(): nonlocal x; x = C(): R4 resolves x.run() to C.run on two C() bindings while k's D() write sits on h. Both resolve the wrong class today. Cause: applyScopeRedirects (calls.ts ~1690-1729) moves each nonlocal write onto the nearest enclosing function that already records a binding of the name, deepest scope first; with no recorded binding (the del is unrecorded) the deeper writer falls back to the nearest function while the other lands on the function that holds the name. Also: def e(): f = m.func plus a nested def g(): f(); del f emits an edge for a call that raises UnboundLocalError. Same family: GCLI-114 (the del gap, filed earlier, item 1) is subsumed by this task; its item 2 (shared gaps of m.attr() and C.m()) stays on GCLI-114.

FIX (on its own task, after the record PR and the leader GO): record every del target (identifier, tuple, list, parenthesised, attribute and subscript targets bind no name) as a binding kind that every rule refuses (kind rebound, like an augmented assignment), in every scope kind including module and class bodies; ALIAS (GCLI-113) already refuses any origin-carrying binding and needs no change. Red/green fixtures per rule: 6d, R4, ALIAS, M1 (module-level instance deleted), LIT, K1 splat deleted, E1 and N3 where they count bindings, rule 5 rebound names, S3 import bindings (del of an imported name). Plus the two reproductions and positive twins.

acceptanceCriteria.text: a del target (a name, a tuple or list of names, a parenthesised name) is recorded as a binding in every scope kind, so rules 6d, R4, ALIAS, M1, LIT, K1, E1, N3 and the rebound-name and S3 import counts refuse a name it deletes, each with a refused fixture asserting no edge leaves the call site and the call stays in its current bin (bin delta against the same source with the call replaced), and a positive twin without the del

THE FIX IS DONE WHEN fixtures A and B go red before and green after: x.run() is not resolved to C.run in either (DEC-303 (a41) item 1, opum-ai/opum-doc#2007). Recording del targets as bindings is necessary ((a40) item 1); if that alone does not turn A and B green, the fix also places each nonlocal write where Python does, in the nearest enclosing function scope that binds the name (the language reference, nonlocal statement), a del target counting as a binding there, with a fixture pinning each placement depth the reproduction exercises. Also the UnboundLocalError input emits no edge, each fixture red before and green after. Route (ii), refusing an origin-carrying binding in 6d and R4, is NOT the fix.

each rule has a mutation check that goes red (equivalent mutants said so), and a per-site five-pin corpus diff against dev is recorded: count and bin moves need no ruling, and every in-repo edge it creates or removes is named per site and sent to the leader for opum-doc before the clear

implementationNotes: DEC-303 (a41), opum-ai/opum-doc#2007, 2026-11-26T09:56:40Z, verbatim: '1. Route (i) is confirmed, and its test is the invariant rather than the mechanism. GCLI-115s fix is done when fixtures A and B go red before and green after: x.run() is not resolved to C.run in either. Recording del targets as bindings is necessary, under (a40) item 1. If that alone does not turn A and B green, the fix also places each nonlocal write where Python does: in the nearest enclosing function scope that binds the name (the language reference, nonlocal statement), with a del target counting as a binding there. A fixture pins each placement depth the reproduction exercises. 2. Route (ii), refusing an origin-carrying binding in 6d and R4, is not the fix. No interim refusal is needed on dev, because nothing releases from dev and (a40) item 3 holds the blind sample until GCLI-115 lands.' ALIAS (GCLI-113) keeps its own refuse-on-origin proviso ((a40) item 4).

BUILD (GO 2026-11-26). Reproduction on origin/dev 04a63e0: sources A and B (sibling writers h2, h3 beside h, k nested in h, x.run() then del x in g) resolve x.run() to C.run before, to nothing after. Recording del targets as rebound bindings (walker case delete_statement, addDeleteBindings in src/python/calls.ts) alone turns both green; applyScopeRedirects is unchanged, no placement fixture needed. Two existing tests that pinned the old del-is-no-binding rule (E1 del of the class name, LIT del) are flipped to refused. Corpus diff vs 04a63e0 on the five pins: flask, jinja, httpx, rich byte-identical; tqdm loses three in-repo edges (tests/tests_synchronisation.py 93:12 and 95:16 to TMonitor.report, 94:5 to TMonitor.exit: monitor = TMonitor(...) with a later del monitor), bins 811/1169/816/311 to 808/1168/820/311. Mutants: 7 of 7 red.

Landed as opum-ai/glyph-cli#180 (squash 6f1dd89): del targets recorded as rebound bindings in every scope kind; fixtures A and B red before and green after; 10 mutants red; corpus diff vs 04a63e0: tqdm -3 in-repo edges (accepted, DEC-303 (a42) item 1), flask, jinja, httpx and rich unchanged; the one created shape off the pins accepted by (a43) item 1.
finalSummary: Walker records every del target as a binding (opum-ai/glyph-cli#180, 6f1dd89). DEC-303 (a40) item 1, (a41), (a42) item 3, (a43) item 1.
